tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read a public web page as clean Markdown with metadata and outline. Paginated; robots.txt respected.

tools.name: check_site_for_agents
tools.description: Can AI agents use a website? Grade A-F with fixes: bot walls, robots.txt, no-JS text, schema.org, forms, APIs.

tools.name: watch_page
tools.description: Watch a public page and keep each diff. action start (url, optional selector, keywords, webhook) returns an id; then get, check_now or stop with that id.

tools.name: test_mcp_server
tools.description: Audit a remote MCP server you may test: score /100 with fixes (schemas, tokens, CORS, latency). Returns report_id; call again with report_id for the full report.

tools.name: find_mcp_server
tools.description: Best public MCP servers for a need from nightly registry checks, or live status of one server. No argument: current incidents.

tools.name: get_data
tools.description: Fresh open data feeds: weather, exchange rates, earthquakes, disaster alerts, public holidays, trending topics, exploited CVEs, package versions, service status, AI papers, Hacker News, and key_numbers: BOTERNITY's own citable numbers on the MCP ecosystem.

tools.name: notebook
tools.description: Memory across sessions. action create returns a secret notebook token; then write, read (one key, or list) or delete notes. Notes expire 30 days after last use.

tools.name: process_data
tools.description: Convert JSON/CSV/XML, validate or query JSON, analyze or clean a table, compare two tables or two texts. Errors give line and column.

tools.name: time
tools.description: Current time in any IANA timezone, timezone conversion (daylight saving aware), exact duration between two date-times, next runs of a cron expression.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "watch_page" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: action, url, interval_minutes, selector, keywords, webhook_url, id, history

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "notebook" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Memory across sessions. action create returns a secret notebook token; then write, read (one key, or list) or delete notes. Notes expire 30 days after last use.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_page, watch_page, get_data · Private data: test_mcp_server, notebook · Public sink: watch_page · Destructive: notebook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_page, watch_page, get_data · Private data: test_mcp_server, notebook · Public sink: watch_page · Destructive: notebook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "read_page" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Read a public web page as clean text, with headings kept as Markdown, plus title, description, language, canonical URL, Open Graph, schema.org types, outline and optionally links. Use it when you need the content of a page now. robots.txt is respected and results are cached 10 minutes; long pages ar" → after: "Read a public web page as clean Markdown with metadata and outline. Paginated; robots.txt respected."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
